dfg-nok.title: Development of complex societies in sub-Saharan Africa: The Nigerian Nok Culture (project results)
dfg-nok.author: Goethe University Frankfurt, Nok project led by Peter Breunig; summary on the DFG GEPRIS project page
dfg-nok.kind: research project summary (primary for the project's own findings)
dfg-nok.rights: Facts and dates cited; no text, images or maps reproduced.
dfg-nok.checked: Opened 26 Oct 2026. Phases 1500-900 BC, 900-400 BC, 400 BC to the turn of the era; almost 500 sites, 84 excavations, 270 radiocarbon dates; iron in the later part of phase 2.

scientia-breunig.title: Professor Peter Breunig: The Significance of Nok Culture Sculptures in Nigerian Prehistory
scientia-breunig.author: Scientia (science communication article about Breunig's research)
scientia-breunig.rights: CC BY 4.0 (stated on the page). Facts cited only.
scientia-breunig.checked: Opened 26 Oct 2026. Start about 1500 BCE; terracottas from the 9th century BCE; sculpture production falls off around 400 BCE; Pangwari and Ifana named.

antiquity-kagarko.title: Exploring the Nok enigma
antiquity-kagarko.author: Nicole Rupp, Peter Breunig and Stefanie Kahlheber, Antiquity Project Gallery 82 (316)
antiquity-kagarko.checked: Opened 26 Oct 2026. Janruwa, Janjala and Akura sites near Kagarko, about 1 km apart; Taruga named as the source of iron smelting evidence.

wiki-nok.title: Nok culture (Wikipedia)
wiki-nok.author: Wikipedia contributors; the facts used cite Shaw 1981 (Scientific American) and Fagg 1969 (World Archaeology)
wiki-nok.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-nok.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-nok.checked: Opened 26 Oct 2026. First terracotta found near Nok village in 1928 in a tin mine; 1943 find recognised by Bernard Fagg; Taruga excavated in January 1961; systematic fieldwork 2005-2021.

wiki-taruga.title: Taruga (Wikipedia)
wiki-taruga.author: Wikipedia contributors; cites Clark (Cambridge History of Africa vol. 2), Isichei 1997, Rupp, Breunig and Kahlheber 2008
wiki-taruga.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only.
wiki-taruga.checked: Opened 26 Oct 2026. Location given only as about 60 km south-east of Abuja. Iron dates disagree: 'firmly dated' to 600 BC (Isichei) versus radiocarbon dates of about the 4th-3rd centuries BC (Fagg's excavation).

wiki-places.title: Coordinates of Nok (Jaba LGA), Kagarko and Katsina-Ala (Wikipedia place articles)
wiki-places.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-places.kind: gazetteer coordinates of modern towns, not of excavated sites
wiki-places.rights: Coordinates are facts; no text reused.
wiki-places.checked: Opened 26 Oct 2026. Nok 9.500 N 8.017 E; Kagarko 9.450 N 7.683 E; Katsina-Ala 7.167 N 9.283 E. Katsina-Ala terracottas described as a Nok sub-style (Fagg, cited via Werness 2003).

gazette-1967.title: States (Creation and Transitional Provisions) Decree 1967, Decree No. 14
gazette-1967.author: Federal Military Government of Nigeria, Gazette Extraordinary No. 37, Part A
gazette-1967.rights: Unknown. Cited and described, not reproduced.
gazette-1967.checked: Read page by page in the agent source check on issue #25 (pages A103-A107): 12 states, schedule by province, a delimitation commission (s.6). Not independently re-read here.

gazette-1976.title: States (Creation and Transitional Provisions) Decree 1976, Decree No. 12
gazette-1976.author: Federal Military Government of Nigeria, Gazette Extraordinary No. 14, Vol. 63, Part A
gazette-1976.rights: Unknown. Cited and described, not reproduced.
gazette-1976.checked: Read in full in the agent source check on issue #25: 19 states, schedule by division and district, a boundaries adjustment commission (s.4); the Kogi area sits in Kwara and the Abuja area in Niger in this schedule. Not independently re-read here.

speech-1996.title: 1996 Independence Day speech (General Sani Abacha), as archived by Archivi.ng
speech-1996.author: Archivi.ng
speech-1996.rights: Site says all rights reserved. Short facts cited only.
speech-1996.checked: Opened 26 Oct 2026. Bayelsa from Rivers, Ebonyi from Abia and Enugu, Ekiti from Ondo, Gombe from Bauchi, Nasarawa from Plateau, Zamfara from Sokoto; before this, a 30-state structure with a Federal Capital Territory.

forumfed.title: Federal Republic of Nigeria (in Constitutional Origins, Structure, and Change in Federal Countries)
forumfed.author: Ignatius Akaayar Ayua and Dakas C.J. Dakas, Forum of Federations Global Dialogue series, Book 1
forumfed.checked: Opened 26 Oct 2026. 12 states in 1967 replacing four regions; seven more in 1976; FCT established in 1976 and the capital officially moved from Lagos in 1991; dates the Mid-Western Region to 1964 (most accounts give 1963).

thisday-1991.title: 5 States Mark 32 Years, Reminisce about Journey So Far
thisday-1991.author: ThisDay
thisday-1991.checked: Opened 26 Oct 2026. Osun, Edo, Kogi, Abia, Yobe, Delta, Jigawa, Kebbi and Taraba created on 27 August 1991 by Ibrahim Babangida.

dailytrust-1987.title: Katsina @30: a dream fulfilled
dailytrust-1987.author: Daily Trust
dailytrust-1987.checked: Opened 26 Oct 2026. Katsina State created from the old Kaduna State on 23 September 1987 by Ibrahim Babangida.

wiki-akwaibom.title: List of governors of Akwa Ibom State (Wikipedia)
wiki-akwaibom.author: Wikipedia contributors; cites Fejokwu 1995, p. 91
wiki-akwaibom.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only.
wiki-akwaibom.checked: Opened 26 Oct 2026. Akwa Ibom created on 23 September 1987 from the south-eastern part of Cross River State.

wiki-statehood.title: List of Nigerian states by date of statehood (Wikipedia)
wiki-statehood.author: Wikipedia contributors; one cited source (Old Naija timeline)
wiki-statehood.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only.
wiki-statehood.checked: Opened 26 Oct 2026. Used only to show disagreement: it says the FCT came from Benue-Plateau, North-Central and North-Western States, and it has clear errors elsewhere (for example Rivers 'from Bendel').

wiki-kogi.title: Kogi State (Wikipedia)
wiki-kogi.author: Wikipedia contributors; cites Pulse Nigeria
wiki-kogi.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only.
wiki-kogi.checked: Opened 26 Oct 2026. Says Kogi was formed on 27 August 1991 from parts of Benue, Niger and Kwara States.

agent-check-25.title: State-creation source check (agent review on issue #25)
agent-check-25.author: Taswira agent workflow, draft PR #39
agent-check-25.checked: Found that the 1967 and 1976 decrees define states by provinces, divisions and districts and set up boundary commissions, so modern state borders are only an approximation for those years.

grid3-states.title: GRID3 Nigeria state boundaries, via geoBoundaries gbOpen NGA ADM1 (boundary year 2022)
grid3-states.author: GRID3; distributed by geoBoundaries (William & Mary geoLab)
grid3-states.rights: CC BY 4.0 (geoBoundaries metadata). Simplified for this page.
grid3-states.checked: Downloaded 26 Oct 2026: 36 states plus the FCT. Simplified to about 12% of points with mapshaper; see history/geo/README.md.

esri-tiles.title: Esri World Dark Gray Base map tiles
esri-tiles.author: Esri, HERE, Garmin, OpenStreetMap contributors and others
esri-tiles.rights: Esri terms of use; attribution shown on the map.
esri-tiles.checked: Same background as the main Taswira map.
